current_leader.name: Merchant settlement acceleration decision engine
current_leader.state_transition: processor balance becomes eligible -> free/standard settlement ETA and paid speed tiers are known -> external bank liquidity and obligations due before each ETA determine actual shortfall -> recommend zero, next-day, same-day, or instant settlement and only the minimum amount -> verify acceleration fees avoided
current_leader.why_survived: Fresh searches found strong evidence that instant payouts remain materially priced and are intended for selective urgent liquidity rather than routine use. Yoco charges roughly 1%-1.5% plus VAT depending on plan and explicitly tells merchants to request the amount they need; MeevoPay Now charges 1.75%; Stripe-linked Dubsado currently lists 1%-1.5% by country; Cashfree starts at 0.30%. Stripe also supports daily, weekly, monthly, and manual payout schedules. No exact product was found that combines PSP balance/ETA, paid speed tiers, live bank cash, and obligations to compute the minimum economically necessary accelerated amount. Exact avoidable-volume evidence is still missing, so leakage remains uncertain rather than passed.
current_leader.closest_threat: First parties already expose amount selection, payout schedules, and speed choices, while banks/treasury products aggregate cash. Novo even offers fee-free faster Stripe access for eligible customers, which economically neutralizes the wedge for that subset. The wedge survives only as a cross-system decision layer that calculates the minimum paid acceleration needed under real obligations.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read-only recommendation using PSP available/instant-eligible balance, standard settlement ETA, fee tiers, bank balance and near-term obligations. Output the cheapest sufficient settlement speed and minimum amount. Do not initiate payouts or hold funds.
current_leader.monetization: Small per valuable decision, low recurring micro-fee, or capped share of verified acceleration fees avoided against a competent cash-management baseline.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: There is still no reliable primary evidence quantifying how much paid accelerated-settlement volume is unnecessary after accounting for genuine liquidity needs. If merchants already accelerate selectively, the recoverable fee pool may be too small.
current_leader.next_research_test: Search for processor disclosures, merchant surveys, payment-company filings, or anonymized transaction studies quantifying instant/same-day payout adoption and merchant liquidity need. Estimate actual acceleration fees minus the minimum fees required to avoid genuine pre-standard-settlement shortfalls. In parallel, search treasury/banking products for exact PSP-balance + bank-balance + obligations + settlement-fee decisioning. Kill if avoidable volume is immaterial or exact functionality is found.

runner_ups.status: survives; adaptive savings beyond competent static tuning remain unproven
survives structurally; still lacks a defensible high-value vertical
survives; leakage magnitude and reconciliation competition remain unresolved

rejections.fatal_flaw: Gate 8 fail: Insurrl already performs the exact per-order decision to skip insurance, rely on carrier coverage, or route to the cheapest valid insurer, with API/store integrations and quantified savings.

Gate 8 fail: PointsOwl already analyzes statements and agreements for missing royalties and rate discrepancies on a 20% success fee; RoyaltyCoPilot, SongBounty and CheckMyRoyalty cover adjacent automated leakage, claiming and underpayment detection.
Gate 8 fail for the basic wedge: CardLockr already provides balance tracking, expiry alerts, APIs/webhooks and team management specifically to stop businesses losing unused gift-card value.

new_search_rules: For optional paid speed products, leakage must be measured against the cheapest liquidity-preserving alternative, not against always using the free rail.

A recommendation wedge fails Gate 8 when a current product already makes the same per-event skip/use/route decision, even if its branding is framed as insurance, royalty, or asset management rather than FinOps.
Primary evidence of behavioral overuse is now required before settlement-acceleration leakage can move from UNCERTAIN to PASS.
